Question ID: CHEM_U02_L07_QZ_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.ATO.04

Stimulus:

RegionRelative wavelengthRelative frequencyRelative energy
Radiolonglowlow
Visible redlonger visiblelower visiblelower visible
Visible violetshorter visiblehigher visiblehigher visible
X-rayshorthighhigh

Question: Which visible color in the table has higher energy, red or violet?

feedback.text: Violet has higher frequency and higher energy than red.
Red has longer wavelength and lower visible energy.
They differ in wavelength/frequency/energy.
Both are visible light.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CHEM_U02_L07_QZ_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.ATO.04

Stimulus:

RegionRelative wavelengthRelative frequencyRelative energy
Radiolonglowlow
Visible redlonger visiblelower visiblelower visible
Visible violetshorter visiblehigher visiblehigher visible
X-rayshorthighhigh

Question: What happens to frequency when wavelength decreases?

feedback.text: Decreasing frequency pairs with increasing wavelength.
It does not become zero from this comparison.
Wavelength and frequency are inversely related.
Mass number is unrelated.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CHEM_U02_L07_QZ_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.ATO.04

Stimulus:

RegionRelative wavelengthRelative frequencyRelative energy
Radiolonglowlow
Visible redlonger visiblelower visiblelower visible
Visible violetshorter visiblehigher visiblehigher visible
X-rayshorthighhigh

Question: Why can spectra help identify elements?

feedback.text: If identical, spectra would not identify elements.
Spectra are light patterns, not mass numbers.
Spectra do not remove protons.

answer.text: Elements can produce characteristic line patterns.

feedback.text: Line patterns can be compared to known element spectra.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CHEM_U02_L07_QZ_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.ATO.04

Stimulus:

RegionRelative wavelengthRelative frequencyRelative energy
Radiolonglowlow
Visible redlonger visiblelower visiblelower visible
Visible violetshorter visiblehigher visiblehigher visible
X-rayshorthighhigh

Question: Which has higher energy, radio waves or X-rays?

feedback.text: Radio waves have long wavelength and low energy.
X-rays have shorter wavelength, higher frequency, and higher energy.
They are not equal in the table.
Relative comparison is possible.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CHEM_U02_L07_QZ_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CHEM.ATO.04

Stimulus:

RegionRelative wavelengthRelative frequencyRelative energy
Radiolonglowlow
Visible redlonger visiblelower visiblelower visible
Visible violetshorter visiblehigher visiblehigher visible
X-rayshorthighhigh

Question: What is wavelength?

feedback.text: Protons are atomic particles.
Neutron mass is not wavelength.

answer.text: Distance between matching points on a wave.

feedback.text: Wavelength measures distance in a wave pattern.
Isotopes differ by neutrons.
